newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Blue chips lift Moroccan bourse higher.
newsitem.headline: Blue chips lift Moroccan bourse higher.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange ended its weekly trading on Friday 0.36 percent higher, lifted mainly by blue-chip companies, brokers said.
The all-share index closed at 479.48 points, up from 477.73 points last Friday.
"The bourse index resumed its upward trend after a slight drop on Thursday...The main reason behind the price surge is lack of paper and liquidity," an analyst at Upline Securities said.
Since the beginning of January demand has remained higher than offers, the analyst said.
In the banking sector, blue chip Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur gained 14 dirhams in one week to close at 414 dirhams, a trader said.
BMCE announced it will cut its interest rate by 0.25 percent on loans starting from February 1, a bank spokesman said.
The interest rate reduction will contribute to the promotion of foreign and domestic investments in Morocco, create new jobs and boost the country's economic growth, he said.
Banque Nationale pour le Developpement Economique was up four dirhams at 153 dirhams. Morocco plans soon to sell its 34.57 percent stake in the bank, officials said.
ONA group, the largest Moroccan conglomerate, jumped 26 dirhams to close at 616 dirhams.
Consumer credit firm Credor, floated on the bourse in December 1996 at an initial price of 385 dirhams, gained 39 dirhams in five days to close at 599 dirhams.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, second largest private conglomerate, remained stable at 565 dirhams.
SNI, which has a market capitalisation of 5.6 billion dirhams, holds diversified stakes in more than 40 firms.
The traded volume on the official market was 60.4 million dirhams from 63.6 million last Friday.
